chunks: And in the narration of Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from some of his men, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

Every adult, male or female, who falsely accuses a minor or an adult, a male or a female, a Muslim, a free person, or a slave, then upon him is the prescribed punishment of slanderous accusation; and upon one who is not yet an adult is the disciplinary punishment.

key_terms.افْتَرَى: falsely accused or fabricated a slander against someone
key_terms.بَالِغٍ: a legally adult person subject to full legal accountability
key_terms.حَدُّ الْأَدَبِ: disciplinary punishment applied short of the full hadd
key_terms.حَدُّ الْفِرْيَةِ: the prescribed legal punishment for slanderous false accusation
key_terms.غَيْرِ الْبَالِغِ: one who has not reached legal adulthood

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an adult or minor who falsely accuses another person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning false accusation, establishing that any legally adult person who commits such slander is liable for the prescribed hadd punishment. If the offender is not yet legally adult, then the response is disciplinary punishment rather than the full prescribed hadd.
